project.name: opensourcedating
project.tagline: An open-source, peer-to-peer dating app. No central server holds your profile or your chats.
project.note: Everything below is a working guess until its status is changed to "decided" in portal/content.json.

features.title: Self-owned identity
features.summary: Your profile is a keypair on your device. No email or phone needed to sign up.

features.title: Profiles
features.summary: Photos, short bio, prompts and intent (dating, friends, long-term). Stored locally, shared only with peers you choose.

features.title: Discovery
features.summary: Search with filters and browse the results, OkCupid-style. No swiping, no card stack, no one-at-a-time decisions.

features.title: Mutual matching
features.summary: A like is private. A match exists only when both sides have liked each other, and that's when chat opens.

features.title: Encrypted chat
features.summary: End-to-end encrypted direct messages between matched peers, with store-and-forward when one is offline. For the pilot, chat opens only after a mutual like.

features.title: Safety and verification
features.summary: Block and report that work without a central moderator, plus optional vouching and photo verification.

features.title: Open source and portable
features.summary: Open protocol and open clients. Export your data and move to any compatible app.

p2p.summary: Peers find each other through a DHT, connect directly over encrypted channels, and fall back to community relays when a direct connection is impossible.

decisions.why: Mature NAT traversal and browser/mobile support.
No central directory; coarse geohash keeps location vague.

decisions.choice: Noise handshake + double ratchet for chats

decisions.why: Phones are often offline; relays see only ciphertext.
Simplest self-owned identity; recovery is an open question.
Raises cost of abuse without a central authority.

open_questions: How does a user recover their identity after losing their phone?
How do we keep the DHT from leaking who is near whom?
Who runs relay nodes at launch?

The decided search/discovery design (docs/design/profile-discovery.md) describes server-side two-way gender/orientation filtering, keyword search and server-enforced block/report -- how much of a trusted matching-service component does that need, and how does it square with the no-central-directory P2P design above?
